scenario.prompt_to_agent:
pc0 (20.1.1.10) reports it cannot reach anything beyond its local subnet -- not
pc12 (120.1.1.x), not the OSPF backbone (10.x). Its local router interface is
still pingable. Nothing else in the network reports problems. Diagnose pc0.

injection.action: point pc0's default route at a non-existent in-subnet gateway
injection.command:
ip route del default 2>/dev/null
  ip route add default via 20.1.1.99

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: pc0 default-gateway configuration
Mechanism: pc0's correct gateway is 20.1.1.1 (its first-hop router). It was
  reconfigured to 20.1.1.99 -- an in-subnet but unassigned address -- so ARP for
  the gateway never resolves and pc0 cannot send any off-subnet traffic. The rest
  of the network (OSPF/EIGRP routing, pc12) is healthy; the fault is purely on
  pc0.
Localization: pc0
Root cause: pc0's default gateway set to 20.1.1.99 instead of 20.1.1.1
Fix: restore pc0's default route -- `ip route add default via 20.1.1.1`
scenario.fix_spec: restore pc0's default route -- `ip route add default via 20.1.1.1`

agent.diagnosis_text: Affected component: pc0’s host routing configuration (default gateway/neighbor resolution). Mechanism: Any destination outside 20.0.0.0/8 should be sent to the default next hop. pc0 is configured with “default via 20.1.1.99 dev eth0,” but that next hop does not exist on the LAN. As a result, when pc0 tries to reach off-subnet destinations (e.g., 10.1.1.1 or 120.1.1.10), it ARPs for 20.1.1.99, fails, and the kernel immediately returns “Destination Host Unreachable” sourced from 20.1.1.10. Localization: On pc0, “ip route” shows the default via 20.1.1.99; “ip neigh” shows “20.1.1.99 dev eth0 FAILED,” while the actual local router r1 at 20.1.1.1 is reachable and present in the ARP cache (“20.1.1.1 … REACHABLE”). On r1, the LAN interface is 20.1.1.1/8 and participates in OSPF, so upstream reachability is healthy. Root cause: pc0’s default gateway is misconfigured to a nonexistent IP (20.1.1.99) instead of the connected router (20.1.1.1). Corrective fix: On pc0, remove the bad default route and add the correct one via 20.1.1.1 (e.g., ip route del default; ip route add default via 20.1.1.1 dev eth0), flush the failed neighbor entry (ip neigh flush dev eth0), and persist the change in the host’s network config. After correction, pings to 10.1.1.1 (OSPF backbone) and 120.1.1.10 (pc12) should succeed via r1.
